_note: Narration script for the ACPO module (CPP-001-AO v4.2, CPPRO-009). Lee voice on eleven_v4, one take, short conversational sentences. The prompt sent to ElevenLabs starts with the [calmly] tag and spells EOC as "E O C", ACPO as "acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema" in full, GTN as "G T N", PDE-5 as "P D E five", and microg as "micrograms"; captions use the text here.

lines.head: Introduction
sentences: Acute cardiogenic pulmonary oedema.
What every Ambulance Officer needs to know.

lines.head: Oxygen and posture
sentences: ACPO is best treated with oxygen and posture.
Sit them up.
High-flow oxygen, through a non-rebreather mask.
And request clinical support.

lines.head: Consult for GTN
sentences: Then consult the EOC Clinician.
They may advise GTN under the tongue.
That's a 300 microgram tablet, or one 400 microgram spray.
But only if the numbers allow.

lines.head: The limits
sentences: The systolic must be over 100.
Exactly 100 isn't enough.
The heart rate must be 60 to 120.
And no PDE-5 inhibitors.

lines.head: PDE-5 inhibitors
sentences: These are mostly for erectile dysfunction.
Sildenafil, vardenafil or avanafil in the last 24 hours? No GTN.
Tadalafil in the last 48 hours? No GTN.
Together with GTN, they can drop the blood pressure dangerously.
So ask, by name, and kindly.

lines.head: After GTN
sentences: Check the vital signs every 3 to 5 minutes.
Repeat GTN only as the EOC Clinician directs.
If anything falls outside the limits, stop and consult again.

lines.head: Get moving
sentences: Provide prompt transport, and notify the hospital.
Sit them up, give oxygen, and GTN only when the numbers allow.
